scenario: AITA for telling my fiance we shouldn't get another bird after we lost ours last night? | Me and my fiance had a lovebird named Rosie. She was the sweetest little thing ever. Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. She called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird, so i tried to stop her saying "no we shouodn't, its a bad idea right now. We just lost Rosie last night" i was upset because not only did i find that not healthy, but i saw it as immediately replacing something we both loved. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

The fiancée starts calling pet shops and shelters to get another bird, even asking her aunt for money. The person tries to stop her, saying it's a bad idea right now because they just lost Rosie. They argue, and the fiancée gets upset, calling them an asshole and saying they have no say in the matter. The person feels they do have a say because they pay the rent and bills, and it's their money that would be used for the new bird. They didn't say never to get another pet, just to wait until they've mourned and their finances improve. So, is the person the asshole here? Let's consider both sides. On one hand, the person is trying to be responsible. They're pointing out that they just lost a pet and that getting another one so quickly might not be healthy for the grieving process. They're also concerned about the financial situation since they're the only one working. It's reasonable to think that replacing a pet so soon could be a way of avoiding the grief rather than dealing with it. Plus, they're worried about the money because they're the primary income earner. On the other hand, the fiancée is grieving and might feel that getting another bird would help her cope. She's dealing with depression, so this loss is hitting her hard. She might see the new bird as a way to fill the void left by Rosie. The person's attempt to stop her could be seen as unsupportive, especially if the fiancée feels like she's being told how to grieve. But wait, the person didn't say they should never get another pet. They just suggested waiting. That's a valid point. They're not being completely unreasonable. However, the way they approached it might have come off as dismissive of the fiancée's feelings. Maybe they could have been more empathetic instead of just saying it's a bad idea. Also, the fiancée's reaction of calling them an asshole and saying they have no say might be over the top, but it's understandable given her emotional state. The person's role in the household as the primary breadwinner does give them some say, especially regarding finances. But they might have handled the situation in a way that made the fiancée feel unsupported. So, is the person the asshole? They have valid concerns about finances and the timing of getting another pet. However, their approach might have been too harsh or insensitive to the fiancée's emotional needs. They could have communicated their concerns more gently, acknowledging her pain while expressing their worries. Instead, they might have come off as dismissive, which could be seen as asshole-ish. But it's also possible that the fiancée's reaction was disproportionate, and the person was just trying to be responsible. It's a tough call because both parties are dealing with a lot of emotions. In the end, I think the person isn't entirely the asshole, but their approach could have been better. They had valid points but might have lacked empathy in the moment. The fiancée's reaction was understandable but perhaps not entirely fair. So, maybe the person is a little bit the asshole, but not entirely.
